title: Plan and share Execution Flows
objective: Let people describe how a change should work, show that plan clearly in the review, and send it only to the Agents that need it.
requirements: Execution Flow is optional. Leaving execution_flows out keeps older flow-free Changes and Slices exactly as they are.

Each Execution Flow names at least one Agent Brief and contains a nested list of steps. Every group says whether its steps must happen in order or may happen in any order. The review always keeps the order in which the steps were written.
Each step uses plain language. It may point to one documented declaration by its exact file path and declaration name, but the link is optional.

One shared module checks all Execution Flow data before SCORE uses it. It rejects malformed flows, unsafe paths, duplicate names or recipients, missing declarations, and unknown Agent Briefs. Invalid flows produce no partial result.

The Accepted Specification is the source of truth for Execution Flows. Every stored copy and every Agent Input must match it exactly, including whether the field was left out and the order of every list.
SCORE stores each flow once and shares that same frozen item only with the Agent Briefs named as recipients. Each Agent receives its flows in the order they were written.
SCORE rejects a compiled plan when its flows, stored items, recipients, or delivery order differ from the Accepted Specification.
Each named Agent receives the complete flow unchanged. Unrelated Agents receive nothing, and preparing or exporting the same plan again produces the same bytes.
The Agent Input and HTML review show only the stored flow data. The HTML places Execution Flow after Context and before Technical record.
Adding, removing, or changing Execution Flow data creates a new frozen revision. Older reviews, approvals, and runs are never rewritten.
An Execution Flow is a written plan for how the code should behave. SCORE does not generate it from source code, and it does not claim that the finished code followed the plan.
